metaTitle: The page's <title> and the title of link previews. Keep "Kando" in Latin letters.
metaDescription: Meta description for search results and link previews. Search results cut it off after about 155 characters in English or about 80 in Chinese, Japanese or Korean, so keep to about 150 to 160 characters in English and 80 to 90 in CJK, in one or two sentences, and say early that Kando plays videos with bilingual subtitles.
metaImageAlt: Description of the link preview image (media/og/<code>.png) for link previews: the app icon and the headline beside the player, which shows the demo film with the original line and its translation.
ogTagline: Short line under the headline on the link preview image (1200×630), the picture shown when the page is shared. One sentence of about 70 to 95 characters in English, 25 to 45 in CJK, so that it fits in three lines. After changing it, make the images again with vp run media in apps/site.
skipToContent: Link for keyboard and screen reader users that jumps past the header to the page's content; visible only when focused.
brandName: The app's name as its interface shows it in your language (mygo.appName in apps/kando/locales): 看懂 in Chinese, Kando in the other languages. Where it is not Kando, the header shows Kando after it.
homeLabel: Accessible name of the brand in the header and footer, which links to the top of this page. Must contain the visible words, brandName and Kando (WCAG label in name).
navLabel: Accessible name of the header's list of section links.
navFeatures: Header link to the four steps (stepsTitle), where what Kando does starts on the page. Keep it short: the four links share one pill.
navCli: Header link to the Command line & MCP section. MCP stays as is. Keep it short.
navOpenSource: Header link to the dark Open source section with the downloads.
languageLabel: Accessible name of the language switcher in the header and of the footer's list of languages. The languages themselves are always named in their own language and are not translated.
githubLabel: Accessible name of the GitHub button in the header, whose visible text is GitHub.
heroTitle: The headline, in two lines: \n (a line break in the JSON string) is where the second starts. Chinese: 原声视频，一句一句看懂。 Say that real videos in their own language become understood one line at a time, and write it as a natural headline rather than a literal translation.
heroTitleMark: The word of heroTitle set in orange, exactly as it is written there (the build fails when heroTitle does not contain it): the word for understanding, which is also what the Chinese name 看懂 means.
heroLead: One or two sentences under the headline: what Kando does with a link, in the order it happens.
heroDownload: Primary button with an Apple logo; it downloads the disk image for a Mac with Apple silicon.
heroOtherSystems: Secondary button next to it, which leads to the download panel's other systems.
heroMeta: Small line under the buttons. {version} is the app's version, such as 0.6.0. MIT stays as is; keep the system names in Latin letters.
heroBadgeTranscribe: Small label on a card floating by the player screenshot, above the words whisper.cpp: the speech is transcribed on the reader's own computer. Keep it to two to four words.
heroBadgeExport: Small label on a card floating by the player screenshot, above the file name video.bilingual.srt, with a check mark: the subtitles have been written to that file.
shotPlayerAlt: Alt text of the player screenshot in the hero; the README in your language has it as the second picture's description.
sitesLead: Line above the scrolling names of websites. {count} is how many websites the app's catalog lists. yt-dlp is a program's name and is written in lower case.
sitesStripLabel: Accessible name of the scrolling list of website names.
stepsTitle: Heading of the four steps a video goes through.
stepDownloadTitle: Step 1 title, under the program's name yt-dlp.
stepDownloadBody: Step 1. The built-in browser is the Browse page of the app's sidebar.
stepTranscribeTitle: Step 2 title, under whisper.cpp: speech becomes text.
stepTranscribeBody: Step 2. The point is that it runs on the reader's own computer.
stepTranslateTool: Small label above step 3's title where the other steps name a program: the AI service that translates. Use the name of the app's AI Service settings in your language.
stepTranslateBody: Step 3. The model can be given the lines before the one it translates, as context.
stepExportTitle: Step 4 title, under the file type .srt.
stepExportBody: Step 4: the two subtitle files, one in the original language and one with both languages.
libraryEyebrow: Small orange line above libraryTitle: the app's word for a library (sidebarLibrary in apps/kando/locales).
libraryTitle: Heading of the Library section, in two lines split by \n.
libraryBody: Text of the Library section. Keep `.kando` between backticks, which set it as code; it is the folder's extension.
libraryPoint1: First point under libraryBody. SRT is the subtitle file format.
libraryPoint2: Second point: a video file on the computer is transcribed where it is, not copied into the library.
libraryPoint3: Third point: each film resumes where it was stopped.
shotLibraryAlt: Alt text of the library screenshot. The README in your language has the same text as its first picture's description; reuse it.
cliEyebrow: Small orange line above cliTitle. MCP stays as is.
cliTitle: Heading of the Command line & MCP section, in two lines split by \n.
cliBody: Text of the section. Keep `kando` and `kando mcp` between backticks: they are commands. MCP is the Model Context Protocol and stays as is; Claude is a product's name.
cliPoint1: {commands} is how many commands the kando tool has. add, list, subtitles, jobs, retry and --json are commands and a flag, and stay as they are.
cliPoint2: {tools} is how many tools the MCP server offers.
cliPoint3: A command started while the app is closed opens it in the background first.
cliTabsLabel: Accessible name of the two tabs of the terminal example.
cliTabCommands: First tab of the terminal example; the second is MCP, which stays as is.
cliCommentAdd: A comment in the terminal example, above kando add <link> --wait. Keep it short, as a shell comment.
cliCommentSubtitles: Comment above kando subtitles <film-id> --format text --translation: print only the translation, for another program to use.
cliCommentStatus: Comment above kando status --json: whether a job can start, and what is missing if not.
mcpCommentAdd: Label above the command that adds Kando to Claude Code, in the MCP tab. Claude Code is a product's name.
mcpCommentTools: Label above the list of the MCP server's tools, whose names stay in English.
detailsTitle: Heading of the nine cards of details: a line you did not understand, heard again.
detailReplayTitle: Card title: replaying the line and looping one line.
detailModesTitle: Card title: the four ways subtitles show.
detailModesBody: Card text: bilingual, original only, translation only and off; the subtitle delay changes in steps of 0.1 seconds.
detailSearchTitle: Card title: searching the lines, and the clips of the side panel.
detailWhisperTitle: Card title. whisper is a program's name and stays in lower case.
detailWhisperBody: Card text. Tiny and Large v3 are the models' names and stay as they are; write the sizes with your language's decimal mark.
detailAITitle: Card title: any AI service you like.
detailAIBody: Card text. Name the providers as the app's AI Service settings do in your language (通义千问 in Chinese, Qwen elsewhere).
detailAILink: Link at the foot of the AI card to everyapi.ai.
detailBrowserBody: Card text. Browse is the sidebar's page (sidebarBrowse in apps/kando/locales); quote it as your language quotes interface names.
detailUploadBody: Card text. R2, S3, OSS and COS are the services' names; write Alibaba Cloud and Tencent Cloud as they write themselves in your language.
detailShortcutsBody: Card text. ⌘/ and ⌘K stay as they are.
detailLanguagesBody: Card text. The five languages are always named in their own language and are not translated.
openEyebrow: Small orange line above openTitle. MIT stays as is.
openTitle: Heading of the dark Open source section. GitHub stays as is.
openBody: Text of the Open source section: Go is the programming language.
openReleases: Button to the list of releases on GitHub.
dlTabsLabel: Accessible name of the macOS, Linux and Windows tabs of the download panel, whose labels stay as they are.
dlMacBody: macOS tab. arm64 and amd64 are in the files' names and stay as they are. Applications is the Finder folder; use its name in your language's macOS.
dlMacButton: macOS tab's main button, with an Apple logo, which downloads the disk image for a Mac with Apple silicon. Apple silicon is Apple's name for its own chips.
dlMacIntel: macOS tab's second button, which downloads the disk image for a Mac with an Intel processor.
dlFirstRun: Note in the macOS and Linux tabs. yt-dlp, ffmpeg and whisper.cpp are programs' names.
dlLinuxBody: Linux tab, before the install command, which ends it, so it may end with a colon. root is the administrator account.
dlLinuxNote: Linux tab, after the command. .deb and apt stay as they are.
dlLinuxButton: Linux tab's button that downloads the Debian package for x86-64 PCs. .deb and x86-64 stay as they are.
dlLinuxArm: Linux tab's button that downloads the Debian package for ARM64 computers. .deb and ARM64 stay as they are.
dlWinBody: Windows tab, before its button. amd64 and arm64 are in the files' names and stay as they are. SmartScreen is Windows' check of downloaded programs; More info and Run anyway are the buttons of its warning, so use their names in your language's Windows.
dlWinButton: Windows tab's main button, which downloads the installer for x86-64 PCs, which most are.
dlWinArm: Windows tab's second button, which downloads the installer for Windows on Arm PCs.
dlWinNote: Note in the Windows tab. PATH is an environment variable and stays as it is.
dlReadme: Link at the foot of the download panel to the README in your language.
copyLabel: Button next to a command that copies it.
copiedLabel: The copy button's label for a moment after it copied.
faqEyebrow: Small orange line above faqTitle; FAQ may stay as is.
faqLead: Line under faqTitle, followed by the link faqAsk.
faqAsk: Link to the repository's issues after faqLead. GitHub Issues stays as is.
faqPriceA: Answer. Ollama and LM Studio are products' names.
faqSitesA: Answer. {count} is the number of websites. Quote the menu item as the app names it in your language (menuGroupHelp › sitesMenuItem in apps/kando/locales).
faqSpeechA: Answer. Hugging Face is a website's name.
faqTranslateQ: Question: what is needed before Kando can translate.
faqTranslateA: Answer. everyapi auth login is a command and stays as is. Name the settings section as the app does (settingsSectionAI in apps/kando/locales).
faqSystemsA: Answer. x86-64 and ARM64 stay as they are.
faqLoginQ: Question: videos a website shows only to people signed in.
faqLoginA: Answer. Quote Browse and Clear Sign-in Data… as the app names them in your language (sidebarBrowse and browseClearData in apps/kando/locales).
faqExportA: Answer: the translation is above the original in the bilingual file.
ctaTitle: Heading of the closing section: start learning tonight, from a video you actually want to watch.
ctaNote: Small line under the closing Download button, followed by the link ctaOther. arm64 and amd64 stay as they are.
ctaOther: Link after ctaNote to the download panel's Windows and Linux tabs.
footerLicense: Footer link to the LICENSE file. MIT License may stay in English.
footerLinksLabel: Accessible name of the footer's list of project links.
footerGitHub: Footer link to the repository. GitHub stays as is.
footerReleases: Footer link to GitHub Releases. Use the name GitHub uses in your language, or keep Releases.
footerIssues: Footer link to the repository's issues, where problems are reported.
notFoundTitle: Heading of the 404 page. One 404 page serves every missing address, so it shows this text in English first and then in every other language with its link home.
notFoundHome: Button on the 404 page back to the home page.
demoLibrary: The library's name under the demo film's title in the hero's player, as the app's screenshots name it in your language.
demoTarget: The language the demo film's subtitles are translated into, in the player's Info tab, named in itself. The English page shows a Spanish translation, as the app's English screenshots do, since English subtitles under an English video would show nothing bilingual.
playerSizeSmall: Subtitle size button in the player's Style tab, after the app's Size heading.
playerSizeMedium: Subtitle size button in the player's Style tab.
playerSizeLarge: Subtitle size button in the player's Style tab.
mcpOther: Note under the MCP tab's tools: other MCP clients run the same command with the argument mcp. mcpServers and mcp stay as they are.
detailModesMark: One or two characters on the orange tile of the Four ways to show subtitles card, standing for bilingual (双 in Chinese). Decorative.
detailLanguagesMark: One or two characters on the orange tile of the Five interface languages card, standing for writing or language (文 in Chinese). Decorative.
demoCue1: Line 1 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue2: Line 2 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue3: Line 3 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue4: Line 4 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue5: Line 5 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue6: Line 6 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue7: Line 7 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
demoCue8: Line 8 of the demo film in the hero's player, the translation of the English line under it (How Rivers Shape Landscapes). Use the translation of the app's screenshots in your language (protoContents in apps/kando/screenshot_prototype_test.go); the English page has the Spanish one.
sitesAll: Link under the works-with strip to the page that lists every supported website. {count} is the number of websites in the catalog, always many.
sitesMetaTitle: The <title> of the supported websites page and of its link previews. Keep "Kando" in Latin letters at the end.
sitesMetaDescription: Meta description of the supported websites page for search results and link previews; about 150 characters in English, 80 in CJK.
sitesPageTitle: Heading of the page that lists every website Kando downloads from, as the app's Help › Supported Websites… sheet names it.
sitesPageLead: Paragraph under the heading of the supported websites page. {ytdlp} is the yt-dlp version the catalog was made from, such as 2026.08.19; {count} is the number of websites.
sitesSearchLabel: Label of the search box of the supported websites page, also read by screen readers as the table's caption.
sitesSearchPlaceholder: Placeholder of the search box: what a reader can type.
sitesColumnName: Header of the table column with the websites' names.
sitesColumnDomain: Header of the table column with the websites' domains, such as youtube.com.
sitesNoMatch: Shown when the search finds no website.
sitesFound: How many websites match the search, beside the search box. {count} can be 0 or 1, so the wording avoids a plural; when it is 0 the table says sitesNoMatch.
modelsEyebrow: Small line above the heading of the whisper models section.
modelsTitle: Heading of the whisper models section. {count} is the number of models the app offers. Keep whisper in Latin letters, lower case.
modelsLead: Paragraph under the heading of the whisper models section: what a small, a large and the recommended model give you, and when the chosen one is downloaded.
modelsAxis: Header of the size column of the models table. Keep MB.
modelsChartLabel: Accessible name of the bubble chart of the models by speed and accuracy, read by screen readers.
modelsChartCaption: Caption under the models chart, which places each model by speed (across) and accuracy (up), with the bubble's area its download size. Says how to read it and that the top right is fast and accurate.
modelsTableCaption: Caption of the table of the whisper models with their speed, accuracy (each rated out of 5) and sizes, which carries the same data as the chart.
modelsColumnModel: Header of the table column with the models' names.
